messages:
alex: Paging gateway suppressed a critical PD page for prod during the late-night window, customers saw 504s on /v1/generate. Noticed from synthetic alerts and some customer reports. :rotating_light:
sre-bot: ALERT: notify_gateway: suppressed page id=pg-98123 rule=suppress-maint start=2026-03-17T06:00:00Z end=2026-03-17T07:00:00Z
mira: @jordan_oncall can you confirm if you got the page? our PD shows no ack for this incident.
jordan_oncall: I didn't get a page. I see PD incident created but no automated page went out. Was expecting an SMS/phone.
alex: logs show suppressor evaluated true because window tz=UTC, but running servers evaluate based on local tz (America/Los_Angeles). Effectively the rule was active too long. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T06:03:12Z suppressor.check rule=svc-maint-2026 tz=UTC result=active
2026-03-17T06:03:12Z pager.dispatch attempt=1 policy=paging-gateway status=suppressed reason=active_suppressor id=pg-98123
2026-03-17T06:03:13Z external.alert synthetic=high-latency route=/v1/generate status=504
```
opslia: Confirmed — the UI shows the suppressor window in UTC. We rolled out a config change last week that stored tz as string but the check reads system tz. Bad mismatch.
mira: Quick mitigation options?
alex: Short-term: disable the suppressor rule for that service and trigger manual PD page. Steps: 1) disable rule in ops console 2) trigger PD via pagerduty-bot manual page.
alex: Command I ran to disable (ops console API):
```
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal/api/suppressor/disable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"rule_id":"svc-maint-2026"}'
```
pagerduty-bot: Manual incident created: PD-INC-7421 assigned to @jordan_oncall, phone/SMS dispatched.
jordan_oncall: Got it, paging now. Confirming I'm oncall and responding. Starting triage on latency spike.
mira: Customer impact: several customers reported timeouts for inference requests in US-W region, estimated 12% of requests in the window timed out. Not a data-loss issue but user-facing errors.
opslia: Launched temporary SMS fallback hook to send to escalation list until suppressor logic is fixed. Hook id=sms-fallback-17Mar.
alex: Root cause hypothesis: suppressor window stored in UTC but runtime compares against server-local tz; edge-case when maintenance windows cross DST boundaries and when servers are in different regions.
mira: Immediate actions: (1) disable offending suppressor (done), (2) verify SMS fallback fired (opslia done), (3) create PD incident and notify accounts (jordan done), (4) rollback the config change that introduced tz-as-string parsing to stable branch.
opslia: Postmortem owners: alex (engineering), mira (product/customer comms), jordan (oncall triage). We'll add automated test for timezone-normalized windows and an alert when suppressor suppresses > 0 pages for high-severity incidents.
jordan_oncall: Triage notes: latency traced to full GPU queue backlog on a single cluster node + prefix cache misses. We're rebalancing traffic while infra team looks at kernel memory churn. No data exfiltration.
alex: Followups for tomorrow: add a lint rule in infra-config to reject timezone strings that aren't canonical IANA names; add a sanity check that suppressor windows align with oncall timezone for the service.
mira: Customer comms draft: "We experienced transient timeouts due to our paging suppressor being incorrectly active; we have mitigated and are investigating. Customers affected received notices. We're prioritizing a fix."
opslia: Will schedule a postmortem doc and include timeline (create doc by EOD). Also adding an alert: if an automated PD incident is created but suppressed, send immediate Slack to #incidents.
alex: Thanks everyone. We'll treat this as P1 for tooling reliability. :thumbsup:
